body.description: Use case: stylized-concept. Style takes priority: STRICTLY chunky toy-block 16-bit pixel art. Every fighter is a tiny faceted block miniature: plain 4x4 square head, 6x4 block torso, two rectangular short legs, 2-pixel arms. NO faces, armor plates, muscles, fabric folds, brick texture, realistic proportions or fine highlights. NO outlines. Each material has ONLY two flat shades. Crisp stair-step square pixels, no gradients or blur. Pale sandy ground, turquoise allies, wine-purple enemies; about 12 colors. Weapons are oversized solid block icons, not detailed objects. Create ONE complete readable tactical fantasy battlefield image, not a sprite sheet or collage. Common comparison scene: an isolated square 8-by-8 board (64 visible cells), shallow isometric view with broad 4:3 diamond tile tops, all edges visible, no perspective vanishing. Three small allied mercenaries occupy the near-left third: shield fighter, longbow archer, dual-dagger rogue. Three hostile fighters occupy the far-right third: broad club wielder, narrow spear wielder, jagged bow wielder. Each figure stands inside ONE cell; weapons and gaps separate silhouettes. Two solid stone blocks interrupt the middle; leave a clear route around them. A single raised floor-spike tile and a separate acid-puddle tile must differ by SHAPE, not only color. One ally has a double-corner selected-cell marker; three empty cells have tiny path dots; one short three-segment health bar is partly empty. Team identity uses round allied bases versus notched hostile bases as well as color. Keep floor calm, characters and hazards highest contrast. No extra actors, mage, scenery, text, numbers, logo, HUD panel, blur, bloom or random pixel noise. Make the actors look like angular wooden building-block toys inside a restrained low-resolution 16-bit game screen, clearly different from normal detailed RPG sprites. 4:3 landscape.
